ai.description: *Sitana spinaecephalus* (Agamidae) reaches 50–60 mm SVL. It is brown with a dorsal diamond pattern and possesses a prominent, elongated nuchal spine and a large, tri-colored dewlap in males.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sitana spinaecephalus* is uniquely identified by the presence of a distinct, elongated, spine-like projection on the posterior edge of its gular fold.
ai.habitat: *Sitana spinaecephalus* inhabits dry, open scrublands and rocky plateaus across the Indian subcontinent, typically found in arid landscapes at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: During the breeding season, males perform rapid, rhythmic displays by extending a vibrant, spiny-edged throat fan to attract females and intimidate rival males.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sitana spinaecephalus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–7 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, typically from April to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sitana spinaecephalus* is endemic to the Deccan Plateau in India, primarily inhabiting dry, open scrublands across Maharashtra, Telangana, and Karnataka.
